description: Address review findings: policy precheck in purchase.execute, walletId bug in PaymentActionService, BigInt-to-Number truncation, clock injection, ApprovalInbox persistence port, and idempotency key default.
steps: Fix purchase.execute to run PolicyPrecheckService before execution instead of hardcoding precheckOutcome: allowed
Fix PaymentActionService.attemptOrderConfirmation to pass walletId not merchantId to kill-switch check - add walletId field to HostedPaymentAction
Fix BigInt-to-Number truncation in PurchaseIntentBuilder.build() by using string representation for max_amount.amount
Add clock injection to ExportService, RecoveryService, and OperationsService
Add persistence port interface to ApprovalInbox
Fix purchase.execute idempotency key to generate a random key when not supplied instead of defaulting to empty string
acceptance_criteria: purchase.execute runs PolicyPrecheckService.precheck() and rejects if denied
PaymentActionService passes correct walletId to kill-switch check
PurchaseIntentBuilder uses string representation for BigInt amount in payload
ExportService, RecoveryService, and OperationsService accept injectable clock parameter
ApprovalInbox defines and uses an ApprovalTaskStore persistence port
purchase.execute generates a random idempotency key when none is supplied
All existing tests continue to pass
verification: source ~/.nvm/nvm.sh && nvm use 22 && cd /root/counterX && pnpm build
source ~/.nvm/nvm.sh && nvm use 22 && cd /root/counterX && pnpm test
findings: MoneyAmount.amount in trust-protocol was changed from number to number | string, requiring a downstream type update in authorization/authority-verifier.ts (perTransactionLimit.amount). All 2777 tests pass. The fs_write tool does not persist to /root/counterX - bash heredocs and sed must be used for file modifications.
